ai.title: Skip bash exit-code wrapper on Windows PTY
ai.summary: Windows skips the bash-style `; ec=$?...` completion wrapper in `runCommandPty` (`npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`). Shell syntax caused failures on cmd/PowerShell; `os.platform() === 'win32'` now sends the raw command. Unix/macOS behavior unchanged.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, it used to add extra instructions that only work in Linux-style shells, which broke things on Windows. Now, on Windows, it just sends your command directly without the extra stuff, while Mac and Linux still get the full explanation of success or failure. If you're on Windows, commands in the terminal will now work more reliably instead of failing due to syntax issues.

ai.title: Restrict terminal usage in system prompt
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to limit `run_terminal_command` tool usage. Added explicit instructions to prefer markdown code blocks for showing commands rather than executing them. Removed dependency installation from primary use cases and added rules against using `cat`/`echo` for file edits and enforcing correct package manager usage.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer installs new software packages on its own when you ask for help, and it's more careful about running commands that could change your system. Going forward, it will prefer to show you terminal commands as text that you can copy and run yourself, rather than executing them directly. This change applies to anyone using the assistant for coding or technical tasks and is already live today.

ai.title: Refine browseraction system prompt and remove type action
ai.summary: Updated system prompt for `browser_action` tool in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Clarified purpose to focus on debugging and visual design. Removed `type` action from available actions list, leaving only navigate, scroll, and screenshot. Adjusted workflow guidance to emphasize localhost development server assumption.

eli5.text: The assistant's ability to look inside your browser has been simplified and made more focused. Previously, it could navigate, scroll, type text into forms, and take screenshots; now it can only navigate, scroll, and take screenshots, and it is specifically told to use these powers for debugging problems and improving visual design. If you let it inspect your browser, you won't see it trying to type into boxes for you anymore, it's also been told to assume your local development environment is already running, so it will be more cautious and less presumptuous about interacting with your site.

ai.title: Expand webscraping tool call prompt
ai.summary: Added instructions to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` clarifying that web scraping returns simplified markdown content. Prompt now explicitly lists use cases: reading documentation pages and other helpful web content. Internal prompt engineering only; no API or model changes.

eli5.text: When someone asks the assistant to grab information from a webpage, the assistant now gets a clearer reminder of what the scraped content looks like: a cleaned-up, simplified version of the page's main text, rather than the full webpage. This makes it easier for the assistant to correctly use that content to read documentation pages or answer questions, and to avoid treating the simplified result as if it were the complete page.

ai.title: Fix claude response storage in backend stream
ai.summary: Corrects accumulation logic in `backend/src/claude.ts` by appending text deltas to the `content` variable instead of the removed `fullResponse`. This ensures the final response object is populated correctly during streaming. Internal backend fix; no user-facing changes.

eli5.text: While the assistant was streaming its response back to you word by word, a behind-the-scenes bookkeeping variable that collected the full reply text got renamed, so the system now stores each chunk of text in the same running total it uses to assemble the final answer. If you were watching the response arrive live, you would see no difference; the fix only corrects how the completed message is recorded for internal use. This is a small housekeeping change that went live today as part of a backend maintenance update.

ai.title: Fix Gemini request saving
ai.summary: Removed `messageId` dependency from save condition in `backend/src/gemini-api.ts`. Replaced manual ID generation with `generateCompactId()`. Ensures messages save when `messages.length > 0` and `userId` is valid, regardless of existing `messageId`.

eli5.text: Conversations you have with the assistant using the Gemini model are now being recorded properly again. Previously, the system waited for a specific tracking number before saving your messages, but that number was sometimes missing, so parts of your conversation were silently lost. Now the system generates its own tracking number and saves your messages whenever there is actual content to store, regardless of whether a tracking number already exists. This fix is live today, so your conversation history should remain intact going forward.
